assumption_inventory: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure. Completeness is derived.
\(P\) is a probability measure on \(E\times\mathbb R\), and its first-coordinate pushforward is exactly \(\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\).
\(p\) is a finite real polynomial, and \((x,y)\mapsto y\) belongs to \(L^2(P)\). No independence is required.
\(S=\{w:\|w\|=1\}\). The display defines the literal predictor \(f_\mu\), potential \(V_\mu\), projection \(G_\mu\), and cost \(c(w,u)=\arccos\langle w,u\rangle\).
\(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) is the set of all probability couplings. The extended nonnegative value \(Q(\mu,\nu)\) is proved finite before interpreting its real square root.
\(C_1,C_2>0\) are uniform over all subsequent probability laws and unit weights, but may depend on \(E,p,P\). No dimension-free or polynomial quantitative bound is asserted.

definitions_and_scopes.objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E; its unit sphere S; standard Gaussian γ; a probability joint law P with Gaussian first marginal and square-integrable response; a finite real polynomial p; arbitrary probability parameter laws μ,ν on S.
definitions_and_scopes.predictor: For every input x, integrate the polynomial feature p(inner(w,x)) against μ on S. This is a literal scalar integral, not only an abstract L² class.
definitions_and_scopes.potential: For every ambient weight w∈E, the literal real potential is 2 times the P-integral of (f_μ(x)-y)p(inner(w,x)). Integrability and existence of its actual ambient gradient are conclusions.
definitions_and_scopes.projection: For unit w, subtract the normal component of the ambient gradient; tangency means inner(w,G_μ(w))=0.
definitions_and_scopes.cost: c(w,u)=arccos(inner(w,u)) on S, and Q is the extended nonnegative infimum of the squared cost over all probability couplings. Finiteness must precede reading sqrt(Q) as a real value.
definitions_and_scopes.quantifier_order: Fix E,p,P and response L² data. Choose positive C₁,C₂ before all probability laws and unit weights. Gradient existence and potential-integrand integrability hold at every ambient weight; tangent/norm/joint law-point estimates concern unit weights.
definitions_and_scopes.constant_dependencies: Constants may depend on E,p,P, including response L² norm, but not μ,ν,w,u. No dimension-free bound or explicit rate is asserted.
definitions_and_scopes.almost_everywhere: Identifications of L² classes with literal predictor/residual are P-a.e.; the resulting scalar potential identity and actual-gradient statement hold for each ambient weight. No common all-weight representative equality is assumed.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Differentiate the Gaussian feature in L2
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Start with \(\Phi(w)(x)=p(\langle w,x\rangle)\) in \(H_0=L^2(\gamma)\). The existing Gaussian derivative theorem constructs its actual Fréchet derivative \(D_0(w)\), a uniform operator bound and an operator Lipschitz bound on the closed unit ball. No feature or derivative witness is an input.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Pull the feature into the joint data space
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The input-marginal identity makes the first-coordinate projection measure preserving. Composition defines a linear isometry \(J:H_0\to H=L^2(P)\), even when response and input are dependent. Set \(F(w)=J\Phi(w)\) and \(D_P(w)=J\circ D_0(w)\). The isometry preserves both operator estimates.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Identify the true parameter average
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Let \(\ell(x,y)=y\) in \(H\) and \(m_\mu=\int F(w)\,d\mu(w)\), a Bochner integral. The existing Gaussian averaging theorem puts the literal predictor in \(L^2(\gamma)\) and identifies its class with the feature mean. Pull back this identity and commute \(J\) with the Bochner integral. Thus \(m_\mu\) is the \(L^2(P)\) class of the predictor, and \(m_\mu-\ell\) represents the residual almost everywhere.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Recover the literal scalar potential
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The residual and every ambient feature belong to \(L^2(P)\), so their product is integrable. The inner product and the almost-everywhere identities identify the literal potential with the displayed ambient function. This function identity is proved inside the theorem.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Differentiate and identify the actual gradient
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Apply the existing quadratic feature-law theorem to \(F,D_P,\ell\) with the bounds just proved. Transport its ambient derivative across the function identity. Uniqueness identifies the displayed vector with the actual ambient gradient of the literal potential at every ambient weight.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Project onto tangent directions
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: For a unit weight, let \(P_wz=z-\langle z,w\rangle w\) and \(G_\mu(w)=P_w\nabla V_\mu(w)\). Substituting the gradient identity lets the feature-law theorem supply tangency and a positive uniform norm constant \(C_1\).

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Keep the angular cost and pass to joint law/point control
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Use \(c(w,u)=\arccos\langle w,u\rangle\) on \(S\), and take the infimum of \(\int c^2\,d\pi\) over all couplings. The feature-law parent proves finiteness of \(Q\) and the projected Hilbert-space estimate. Substitute the actual-gradient identity for both laws. The constants \(C_1,C_2\) precede every law and weight quantifier; they may depend on \(E,p,P\), including the response norm.

missing_bridges_to_check: The Gaussian derivative theorem must give global ambient differentiability while only requiring bounded/Lipschitz derivative estimates on the closed unit ball.
The pullback must use the actual first-coordinate map and the exact P.map fst = γ identity; no response/input independence may enter.
Every μ is a probability law on the unit sphere. The literal predictor-to-feature-mean bridge and commutation of J with Bochner integration require the relevant integrability facts.
L² identities only hold a.e.; the proof must legitimately pass them through integrals and obtain equality of scalar functions for every ambient w before transporting the derivative.
The gradient must be the library actual ambient gradient, identified by derivative uniqueness rather than left as an assumed witness.
The coupling set must consist of all probability couplings with μ and ν marginals. Q must be finite and the real/extended-real square-root convention must be explicit.
C₁,C₂ must precede μ,ν and unit points; all dependence on Gaussian feature bounds and response norm must remain within E,p,P.
Dimension zero gives an empty unit sphere, so universal claims over probability laws on it are vacuous; no unlisted nonempty-dimension hypothesis should appear.
